subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` as the supported explicit escape hatch for early provider recovery, and is a terminal-only recovery path acceptable?
rationale: The code can be assessed mechanically, but choosing a permanent public auth-state mutation command versus guided or automatic recovery requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Approve escape hatch with proof
options.body: Adopt the profile-scoped command as a low-level recovery API, require redacted end-to-end runtime evidence, and track a Doctor or in-product Fix surface for non-technical users.

options.title: Move to guided recovery
options.body: Rework the change around Doctor, Control UI, or another visible recovery action rather than establishing a terminal-only public command.

options.title: Rely on automatic recovery
options.body: Close or redesign the PR if early recovery should be handled exclusively by runtime probes and fallback policy without manual state mutation.

recommendation.title: Approve escape hatch with proof
recommendation.body: Adopt the profile-scoped command as a low-level recovery API, require redacted end-to-end runtime evidence, and track a Doctor or in-product Fix surface for non-technical users.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal combines major auth-profile invariant work with merger responsibility for related cooldown behavior.
